plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered flower heads in many forms, including pompon, spider, and decorative types. It thrives in the cool, short days of autumn and is a staple of fall gardens across the Northern Hemisphere.
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; native to East Asia, especially China and Japan
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums have been cultivated in China for over 2,000 years and are the national flower of Japan, where the Chrysanthemum Throne symbolizes the imperial family.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, graceful tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In late October its blooms carpet streets and gardens with purple petals across the Southern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa (Pretoria), Argentina, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacarandas earned it the nickname 'Jacaranda City', and an old local tradition says a petal falling on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial whose pink-lilac, crocus-like flowers emerge from bare ground in autumn, long after the leaves of the previous spring have died back. It grows in damp meadows and woodland edges.
plants.location: Native to Europe, from Britain and Ireland to the Balkans; naturalized in parts of North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a true crocus. It is highly toxic, but it is the natural source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to double chromosome numbers.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: A delicate annual with feathery foliage and daisy-like flowers on tall, slender stems. In warm regions such as Mexico, its native range, and in mild-autumn gardens it continues blooming until the first hard frost.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer to late autumn; peak in Mexico during the autumn rainy season's end
plants.location: Native to Mexico and the southwestern United States; cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: Cosmos comes from the Greek word 'kosmos', meaning 'order' or 'harmony', and the flowers are a favorite of pollinators including monarch butterflies during their autumn migration to Mexico.
